inputFacts.title: Michigan voters can request absentee ballots for November election
inputFacts.summary: Voters in Michigan can spoil already submitted absentee ballots by submitting a written request to their local clerk's office. Requests must be signed and specify whether a new ballot should be mailed or picked up in person. The deadline for requests is 5 p.m. on October 23 for the November election. Voters who cast ballots at early voting sites or polling locations cannot spoil their ballots.

inputFacts.title: Grammy Award-winning singer Samara Joy performs at Hill Auditorium
inputFacts.summary: Grammy Award-winning jazz singer Samara Joy performed at the University of Michigan’s Hill Auditorium as part of her 2026 world tour promoting her upcoming EP. The concert, organized by the University Musical Society, featured songs from her albums and a preview of her new EP, with Joy emphasizing the preparation and chemistry of her septet. Attendees praised the emotional and enlightening experience of witnessing her live performance.

inputFacts.title: Detroit-based singer-songwriter Christian Ohly is finding his way back to the light
inputFacts.summary: Detroit-based indie-folk artist Christian Ohly is hosting an album release party for his second full-length, *Light Again*, on Oct. 23 at the Magic Bag in Ferndale. The event marks a pivotal moment in his decade-long Michigan music career, reflecting his growth as a songwriter and performer influenced by artists like The Head and the Heart and Dan Zott of Jr. Jr.

inputFacts.title: Newly counted ballots mean Hamtramck's mayor may have actually lost last year's election
inputFacts.summary: Nearly a year after Hamtramck Mayor Adam Alharbi won his 2025 mayoral race by 11 votes, an additional 37 ballots discovered after the election have reversed the results, giving opponent Muhith Mahmood a 12-vote lead. The Wayne County Board of Canvassers counted the ballots following legal challenges, but Alharbi has filed a lawsuit alleging Mahmood doesn't meet residency requirements. A hearing on this issue is scheduled for October 22, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Fact check: Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers debate Trump, tariffs, war, more
inputFacts.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers engaged in a heated debate in Grand Rapids, clashing over tariffs, the Iran war, personal wealth, and policy positions. The candidates are vying to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters in a race that could determine Senate control during Trump's final term. Fact checks address claims about tariff impacts, medical credentials, and financial ties.

inputFacts.title: Michigan advocates work to ease election security anxieties as Nov. 3 approaches
inputFacts.summary: With two weeks remaining until the Nov. 3 general election, Michigan advocates and nonprofits are addressing election security concerns through outreach, legal protections, and transparency efforts. Experts emphasize the state's decentralized election system as a security safeguard while monitoring potential federal interference and mail-in voting challenges. Organizations like Common Cause and the Michigan Election Observation Project are deploying hotlines, observers, and educational campaigns to ensure voter confidence.

inputFacts.title: How to register to vote in Michigan
inputFacts.summary: The article outlines eligibility requirements and registration methods for voting in Michigan, including in-person, online, and mail options. Voters must be U.S. citizens, Michigan residents for 30 days, and at least 17½ years old. Registration deadlines and required documentation are detailed for the November election.

inputFacts.title: Commerce Township-based Outrun Hunger to host ‘Sweet 16 Running Strong’ 5k and 1-mile run to combat hunger
inputFacts.summary: Outrun Hunger, a Commerce Township nonprofit, is hosting its 16th annual 5K and 1-mile run/walk on November 14 to combat hunger. The event has raised over $308,000 since 2011, helping nearly 12,000 families through local food pantries. Participants can register for races, volunteer, or donate, with prizes and sponsor gifts available for early registrants.
